requirement: Register users with a normalized email and a salted scrypt password hash, reject duplicates with 409 and short passwords with 422, and return only id and email from both signup and lookup by declaring a public response_model.
skeleton: UserIn, UserRecord and UserOut pydantic models, an in-memory USERS dict with reset_db, hash_password using hashlib.scrypt with a random salt, and POST /users and GET /users/{user_id} returning records filtered through response_model=UserOut.
caption: Hiding stored secrets with FastAPI response models. UserIn requires an email of 3 to 254 characters and a password of at least 8 characters via pydantic Field, so shorter passwords get a 422. UserRecord adds an integer id and a password_hash; UserOut exposes only id and email. hash_password(password, salt) runs hashlib.scrypt with n=2**14, r=8 and p=1 and returns the salt, a dollar sign and the hex digest. POST /users is declared with response_model=UserOut and status 201: it strips and lower-cases the email, raises HTTPException 409 with detail email already registered when that address exists, and stores a UserRecord whose salt comes from secrets.token_hex so identical passwords hash differently. GET /users/{user_id} returns the stored UserRecord or raises 404; both handlers return the full record and rely on response_model to drop password_hash from the JSON. The fixture asserts that signing up with spaces and capitals returns 201 and exactly the id and lower-cased email, that the lookup body has no hash and an unknown id is 404, that stored hashes contain a dollar sign, never the password, and differ between users, that a case-variant duplicate gets 409, and that a seven-character password gets 422.

plan.intent: Let people sign up without ever leaking their password hash
constraints: Responses contain only id and email
Emails are trimmed and lower-cased before storage and duplicate checks
A duplicate email raises HTTPException with 409
Passwords shorter than 8 characters are rejected with 422
Each password is hashed with scrypt and its own random salt

rationale.teaches: Returning an internal model while response_model declares the public schema, plus normalized uniqueness checks and per-user salts.
rationale.why: Handlers that reuse the storage model as the response model leak secrets silently, and case-sensitive duplicate checks or fixed salts pass casual tests, so the fixture compares exact bodies and hashes across users.

ops.docstring: User signup API whose responses never expose the stored password hash.

ops.stmt: from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, status

params.name: UserRecord
params.doc: Stored user, including the salted password hash.

ops.source:
def hash_password(password: str, salt: str) -> str:
    """Return salt and scrypt digest joined by a dollar sign."""
    digest = hashlib.scrypt(password.encode(), salt=salt.encode(), n=2**14, r=8, p=1)
    return f"{salt}${digest.hex()}"

candidates.why_wrong: The lookup declares UserRecord as its response model, so password_hash is returned to clients.
Emails are stored as typed, so capitals survive and case-variant duplicates are accepted.
Every user shares one fixed salt, so identical passwords produce identical hashes.
Signup keeps the default 200 status instead of 201 Created.
The minimum length is 6, so a seven-character password is accepted.
